title: U.S. House · Texas's 24th Congressional District
area: North Texas suburbs of Dallas-Fort Worth, including Irving, Coppell, and parts of Denton, Tarrant, and Collin counties.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.
In the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff, Kevin Burge defeated TJ Ware, 78.1% to 21.9%, to advance to the general election.

summary.text: Beth Van Duyne is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 24th District, first elected in 2020. Before Congress she served on the Irving City Council, as Mayor of Irving, and as the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's Southwest regional administrator, and she also worked as a consultant. She serves on the Ways and Means Committee and chairs a Small Business subcommittee, and was unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Lives in Irving, Texas, which her official biography says has been her home for over 30 years.
Earned a B.A. in city/regional planning and government and law from Cornell University, graduating magna cum laude according to her official biography.
Worked with startups, mid-size companies and Fortune 500 corporations and ran a consulting business, according to her official biography.

Served on the Irving City Council from 2004 to 2010, then as Mayor of Irving from 2011 to 2017; her official biography says she was the first woman elected mayor of the city. She won re-election as mayor in 2014, defeating Herbert A. Gears.

Was appointed in 2017 as Regional Administrator of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's Southwest Region, overseeing HUD programs in Arkansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Texas under Secretary Ben Carson.
Is a former board member of the Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, according to her official biography.

Won the open 24th District seat in the November 3, 2020 general election, defeating Democrat Candace Valenzuela and three others; she took office January 3, 2021 and succeeded Kenny Marchant. She was re-elected in 2022 with 59.7% (over Jan McDowell) and in 2024 with 60.3% (over Sam Eppler).

Serves on the Ways and Means Committee, with seats on its Oversight, Tax, Trade, and Work and Welfare subcommittees; chaired the Small Business Subcommittee on Oversight in the 118th Congress and chairs the Small Business Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access in the 119th.

Was unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 71,506 votes. Her official biography says she is the mother of two and was the second Republican woman from Texas elected to the U.S. House.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Small Business (Chairman, Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access subcommittee) and the House Committee on Ways and Means (Oversight, Tax, Trade, and Work and Welfare subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Kevin Burge
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff with 78.1% of the vote

summary.text: Kevin Burge is the Democratic nominee challenging Rep. Beth Van Duyne. He is a U.S. Marine Corps Reserve veteran and former Defense Intelligence Agency employee who later served as technical advisor for the White House Situation Room renovation, and this is his first run for office as far as Ballotpedia's records show. He won the Democratic primary runoff over TJ Ware on May 26, 2026, 78.1% to 21.9%.

background.text: Was born into a working-class family in Los Alamos, New Mexico, and says his family later settled in North Carolina.
Enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps at 17 after the September 11 attacks; Ballotpedia lists his service in the Marine Corps Reserve from 2003 to 2011.
According to his campaign website, he served two deployments to Iraq, including as a logistician, and later deployed to Kabul, Afghanistan, leading a security team escorting intelligence analysts.
Earned a master's degree in sustainable development from North Carolina State University.
Worked at the Defense Intelligence Agency, then worked in the intelligence community and served as technical advisor for the White House Situation Room renovation during the Biden administration.
Lives in North Richland Hills with his wife, a Texas Army National Guard officer who came to the U.S. from Honduras as a child, and their son.
Led the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 48.0%, then won the May 26, 2026 runoff over TJ Ware with 78.1% of the vote.

priorities.text: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey, named affordability as the district's main challenge, citing housing, healthcare, childcare, and utility and insurance costs.
Said he would work in Congress to roll back tariffs, expand grants for technical skills training, and fund universal pre-K.
Listed foreign policy priorities of strong global alliances, restoring congressional war authority, and congressional oversight of trade and military action.

positions.summary: Says he would work to roll back tariffs imposed under the Trump administration, citing their inflationary effects.
positions.quote: I'll work to roll back Trump's Tariffs and their inflationary effects

positions.summary: Says he would fund programs such as universal pre-K.
Lists universal healthcare among the public policy areas he is personally passionate about.
